title: Closed real intervals are compact
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For arbitrary real numbers $a,b\in\mathbb R$, the closed interval $[a,b]=\{t\in\mathbb R:a\le t\le b\}$, with the subspace topology from the usual topology of $\mathbb R$, is compact: every open cover has a finite subcover. The interval is allowed to be empty.
